key_insight: Using phase-flip-biased ancilla qubits can make QLDPC syndrome extraction circuits less prone to hook errors and short-loop issues, improving fault tolerance even without perfect bias.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a practical hardware-aware path to better quantum error correction performance for scalable QLDPC-based systems when ancilla noise can be made strongly asymmetric.
method: Analyzed syndrome extraction for general QLDPC circuits under biased ancilla noise.
Compared conventional ancilla noise to phase-flip-only and strongly phase-biased cases.
Evaluated bicycle bivariate codes and a cyclic hypergraph product code for fault-distance and Tanner-graph loop structure.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports up to nearly an order-of-magnitude improvement in logical error rate at circuit noise of 2×10^-3 when ancilla bit-flip errors are 50× less likely than phase-flip errors.
watch_item: The benefit depends on maintaining strong ancilla noise bias; if hardware cannot reliably suppress bit-flip errors, the improvement may be reduced.
paper_title: Untangling QLDPC Codes with Biased Noise Ancilla
